answer: Sybil resistance can be grown, not declared: the protocol kernel plants a few seeded canary answers each epoch, trapdoors hidden like shafts in karst terrain. Honest graders read every text and step around them; copy-farms never read, they harvest and replay, so their submissions sprout as identical vines across thousands of wallets. One caught vine costs the slashed stake of every root it grew from, while careful graders earn from the same canaries. Copying stops paying the moment imitation is measurable, and an economy that grades what it reads no longer needs to trust who signs.
